questions.question: This is ___ most interesting chapter in the book.
questions.explanation: The superlative 'most interesting' identifies one chapter as the highest in degree.

questions.question: She was ___ first person to reach the finish line.
questions.explanation: Ordinal numbers such as first, second and third normally take 'the' when identifying a position in a sequence.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: He is tallest player in the team.
He is the tallest player in the team.
He is a tallest player in the team.
He is an tallest player in the team.
questions.correctAnswer: He is the tallest player in the team.
questions.explanation: The superlative 'tallest' identifies the player with the greatest height in the group.

questions.question: This is ___ second time I have visited this museum.
questions.explanation: Ordinal numbers used to indicate an order or occurrence normally take 'the'.

questions.question: Which option correctly completes the sentence? Mount Everest is one of ___ highest mountains in the world.
questions.explanation: The superlative phrase 'highest mountains' takes 'the', even after 'one of'.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: This is ___ least expensive option available.
questions.explanation: The superlative expression 'least expensive' normally takes 'the'.

questions.question: Which sentence is correct?
questions.explanation: Names of days used in their ordinary calendar sense do not take an article.

questions.question: He finished in ___ third position.
questions.explanation: The ordinal number 'third' takes 'the' when indicating a specific position.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly compares two candidates without using a superlative?
options: She is the better of the two candidates.
She is a better of the two candidates.
She is best of the two candidates.
She is the best of the two candidates.
questions.correctAnswer: She is the better of the two candidates.
questions.explanation: When comparing exactly two people or things, the comparative 'better' can take 'the' to identify the one with the advantage.

questions.question: This is ___ most useful tool for the task.
questions.explanation: The superlative 'most useful' identifies the tool considered highest in usefulness in the given context.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: She is the happiest when she is painting.
She is happiest when she is painting.
She is a happiest when she is painting.
She is an happiest when she is painting.
questions.correctAnswer: She is happiest when she is painting.
questions.explanation: A superlative adjective used predicatively to describe a state or feeling can appear without 'the'.

questions.question: The library is on ___ fourth floor of the building.
questions.explanation: Ordinal numbers identifying a particular floor take 'the'.

questions.question: Complete the expression: ___ sooner we start, ___ better it will be.
questions.explanation: The paired comparative structure 'the sooner..., the better...' uses 'the' before both comparative forms.
